chapter: Decca records, the Savoy and Moe Gale
title: Arriving at the Savoy in 1941 with the Sultans
summary: They opened at the Savoy Ballroom in 1941, after Chick Webb's death, playing a private party and then alongside the Sultans.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: they just ate it up so then we went on to New York, and Tim Gail came in and caught us at Gary and he sat and we talked and he says well, we're going to bring you guys on into New York at the Savoy Ballroom and going to try to do some business together and do somethings and we talked okay. And so they did. They brought us on in there and --
What date about was this? What year, I mean.
This was 1941, I believe. I believe this was '41, yes.
Yes, that's right. Chick Webb had passed. That's true. And --

And we opened there, I forget, we played for, I think the first night we were there, we played for some kind of private party or something like that and I don't remember what band was in there with us that first night that we played but it was sort of a private party.

And then the next night I think they started the Sultans with us, and the Sultans was a kicking little old group, you know, the Sultans they was kicking. Okay. We handled the Sultans but I always used to have to tell the cats, okay, cats, better watch this stuff, now watch it, because sometimes we take 30 and a 20 and sometimes those cats awful groove, are

you listening, but then the next week they brought us in with Lucky. Now, Lucky could have been the first group that we came in with, but I'm not sure, but it was either the first or second but anyway --
They very often had the Sultans and two big bands.
Scoops Cary, wasn't he in the Sultans.
